summary: The Beach is a 2000 English-language drama film directed by Danny Boyle, adapted by John Hodge from Alex Garland's 1996 novel of the same name. It stars Leonardo DiCaprio, Tilda Swinton, Virginie Ledoyen, Guillaume Canet and Robert Carlyle, and was filmed on the Thai island Koh Phi Phi. The note also covers the controversy over 20th Century Fox altering the natural beach of Ko Phi Phi Leh, including lawsuits by environmentalists and the lasting damage until the 2004 tsunami.
one_line: The Beach is a 2000 Danny Boyle film shot on Koh Phi Phi, notable for the environmental damage caused by 20th Century Fox's beach alterations.
key_facts: The Beach is a 2000 English-language drama film directed by Danny Boyle.
The Beach is based on the 1996 novel of the same name by Alex Garland.
John Hodge adapted Alex Garland's novel for the film.
The film stars Leonardo DiCaprio, Tilda Swinton, Virginie Ledoyen, Guillaume Canet, and Robert Carlyle.
The film was filmed on the Thai island Koh Phi Phi.
20th Century Fox bulldozed and landscaped the natural beach setting of Ko Phi Phi Leh to make it more 'paradise-like'.
The production altered some sand dunes and cleared some coconut trees and grass to widen the beach.
Fox set aside a fund to reconstruct and return the beach to its natural state.
Environmentalists filed lawsuits, arguing the ecosystem damage was permanent and restoration attempts had failed.
After shooting, a clear flat area at one end of the beach remained, created artificially with an odd layout of trees that was never rectified.
The beach area remained damaged from its original state until the tsunami of 2004.
